en: The Legend of the Elder Dhammacakkika Kuṇḍadhānavagga, Number 9 I was a wheelwright in the city of Benares, and I fashioned wheels for chariots. At that time, the Buddha Kassapa, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One, appeared in the world. Having heard of his fame, I went to see him. Having approached the Teacher, I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, who was like a mountain of gold. With palms joined in reverence, I paid homage to the Conqueror and sat down to one side. Then the Teacher, knowing my disposition, taught me the Dhamma in its various aspects. Having heard the Dhamma from the Buddha, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Then, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, I made a vow regarding the Victor. "May I become a wheel-turning monarch in the future, and may I meet with this very Buddha. When I had made this vow, the Teacher smiled. Then, asked by Ānanda, the Buddha explained the reason for his smile. "This wheelwright here has made a vow; in the future he will become a wheel-turning monarch named Dhammacakkika. Having heard these words of the Buddha, I was filled with joy and great happiness. Then, having honored the Teacher, I departed from his presence. In the dispensation of the Buddha Gotama, I was reborn in a wealthy family. When I grew up, I became a master of the three Vedas and all branches of knowledge. I was skilled in the sixty-four arts and possessed the five supernormal powers. I was well-versed in the eighteen sciences and was a teacher of the Vedas. I was a reciter of the Three Vedas, a master of the six Vedāṅgas, and a knower of the meanings of the scriptures. I was a teacher of the Brahmins, honored and respected by the people. Then, having heard the fame of the Buddha, I went to the Jetavana Grove. Having approached the Teacher, I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, who was like a mountain of gold. With palms joined in reverence, I paid homage to the Conqueror and sat down to one side. Then the Teacher, knowing my disposition, taught me the Dhamma in its various aspects. Having heard the Dhamma from the Buddha, I attained the fruit of non-returning. Then, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, I made a vow regarding the Victor. "May I become a wheel-turning monarch in the future, and may I meet with this very Buddha. When I had made this vow, the Teacher smiled. Then, asked by Ānanda, the Buddha explained the reason for his smile. "This monk here has made a vow; in the future he will become a wheel-turning monarch named Dhammacakkika. Having heard these words of the Buddha, I was filled with joy and great happiness. Then, having honored the Teacher, I departed from his presence. By means of that wholesome deed, I have now attained the fruit of arahantship. I am free from birth, aging, and death; I have done what was to be done. There is no further existence for me beyond this. Thus did I speak these verses in praise of the Elder Dhammacakkika. This is the legend of the Elder Dhammacakkika.
“In the presence of the lion-throne of the Blessed One Siddhattha,
the Wheel of Dhamma was established by me.”
Well-made and praised by the wise,
I shine with a beautiful form, possessing my own yoke,
strength, and vehicle.
Many people constantly follow and attend upon me,
with sixty thousand musical instruments.
I always have attendants;
I shine with a retinue—
this is the fruit of meritorious deeds.
In ninety-four aeons ago,
the wheel that I established— since then,
I have never known an evil rebirth.
This is the fruit of the Wheel of Dhamma.
Eleven aeons ago,
there were lords of men who stood [in sovereignty];
By the name Sahassara,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
[He attained] the four analytical knowledges.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Dhammacakkika speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Dhammacakkika, the ninth.
